GEM has CC1, timepoint 1 at 800 MW, pre-construction, start 2030. One combined cycle block is one GEM unit, so the gross total is about 837.9 MW. *.text: Scope-wide: read the Bundesnetzagentur award list for the first capacity tender of September 2026 (published 3 November 2026, https://www.bundesnetzagentur.de/DE/Fachthemen/ElektrizitaetundGas/Kapazitaetsmarkt/Ausschreibung/Gebotstermin_Sep26/_DL/Zuschlagsliste.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=3). Eleven bids won, 5,160 MW in all. Match every awarded unit to a GEM plant. Two awards have no GEM gas plant: LEAG Gaskraftwerk Boxberg 10 (SEE998894554863) and Boxberg 20 (SEE913385327436), each 560 MW gross, in Saxony, planned for 30 September 2031. Boxberg power station (L100000101978) is a coal plant in the unfiltered export. Stage each as a new unit at that plant, or a new plant if a source places it elsewhere, with LEAG as owner. An award is a capacity contract, not a construction start. It does not change the status on its own; the status follows the lifecycle rules (a permit application or approval means pre-construction, otherwise announced). Put the award in Status Detail, added above the existing text, with the award list as the link. Record gross electrical capacity, never the net figure. The award takes effect on 10 November 2026.

Scope-wide: list every GEM gas unit in Germany that is announced, pre-construction or construction and is not on the 3 November 2026 award list. For each, look for the owner's statement on whether it bid and what happens next. Losing or not bidding is not a status change; record it in Status Detail only when a source says it.

Scope-wide: data centers. Germany's data center hubs (Frankfurt am Main and the Rhine-Main area, Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Düsseldorf and Cologne) have campuses whose diesel or gas backup generators add up to 20 MW or more. Fleets this size usually need a permit under the federal emissions control law (BImSchG) from the state authority, and town planning records often name them first. Search the state permit records and town planning records for each large campus, sum the generator nameplate in electrical MW, and stage every fleet at 20 MW or more as a new plant with Backup Power yes. GEM already has Frank Cube, IQ Energy Center, KMW Gas Engine Power Plant and Mainz power station.

Scope-wide: the LNG team's captive sheet lists three German terminals with no GEM captive plant: Brunsbüttel (T100000130460), Mukran (T100000131141) and Wilhelmshaven (T100000130458). Mukran was answered in October as engines on the floating regasification ship, 39.9 MW. Check each for generator sets of 20 MW or more of electrical nameplate. Compressor drives do not count.

Scope-wide: the October batches could not read 111 pages. A retry on 4 November 2026 (batches/germany-redo/october_giveups_retry.md) opened 23 of them. For every page that now opens, use it where the plant's task needs it. For each page still gone or with a dead host, run the address through fetch.py and a Wayback Machine lookup before calling it dead. A page that opened but did not show the value is a research answer, not an access failure; say so in the plant's note.
